Date Filter — Prototypes

Five takes on the "+ Date filter" control from the spending report, in the same dark-glass theme. Everything below is wired up with vanilla JS so you can actually click around — nothing is connected to real data.

1. Pills + Select 2. Quick Range Popover 3. Timeline Scrubber 4. Searchable Checklist 5. Preset + Custom Range 6. Structured + Drill Calendar 7. Structured + Native Dates
Option 1
Quick Pills + Grouped Native Select

The smallest possible change from what exists today. Adds a row of one-click range pills (This Month / Last 3 / Last 6 / YTD / All Time) above the existing dropdown, and groups the select's months by year instead of one long flat list. Cheapest to build, easiest to scan, no new interaction patterns to learn.

Active: No date filter applied
Option 2
Quick-Range Popover with Month Grid

One button opens a small panel: presets on top for the common cases, then a year-tabbed grid of months below for anything custom — click multiple months to multi-select, hit Apply when done. Good balance of speed (presets) and precision (grid) without leaving the toolbar.

Active: No date filter applied
Option 3
Interactive Timeline Scrubber

Every month in your data plotted along a single track. Drag either handle — or click a tick to snap the nearest one — to pick a continuous range. Feels native to a finance app (think stock-chart range selectors) and makes the size of your data window immediately visible, at the cost of being awkward for non-contiguous selections.

Drag a handle, or click any tick to move the closer one
Active: No date filter applied
Option 4
Searchable Multi-Select Checklist

A checkbox list grouped by year (click a year header to collapse it), each row showing that month's total as a preview, with a search box up top for jumping straight to a month by name. Best option if people tend to build up non-contiguous selections (e.g. "every December") rather than a single range.

Option 5
Preset Dropdown with Custom Range Builder

A single button that always shows the current selection as its label (e.g. "Last 6 Months"). Opening it shows a flat list of presets plus a "Custom Range…" item that swaps the panel for two From / To month pickers. Reads the most like a familiar analytics-tool date picker (Stripe, GA, etc.) and keeps the toolbar itself minimal.

Active: No date filter applied
Round 2 — built from a detailed interaction spec
Option 6 · Round 2
Structured Categories + Drill-Down Calendar

Everything — This/Last presets, individual months, and a custom range — stages into one pending list and only becomes a chip when you hit Apply; nothing is special-cased or auto-closes early anymore. This/Last Quarter and Year each collapse into a single compact chip; clicking individual months in the grid adds one chip per month (the same entry either way, so clicking "This Month" and then that month's cell is a no-op, not a duplicate); Start/End becomes one range chip. Clear only unselects months (grid picks + This/Last Month); Clear all filters wipes everything and closes. Start/End use a drill-down calendar: click the month or year in the header to zoom out to a month grid or a paginated year grid, then click a cell to drill back in.

Option 7 · Round 2
Structured Categories + Native Date Inputs

Identical popover to Option 6 — same This/Last rows, same year-tabbed month grid, same pending/Apply/Clear model — but Start/End are plain <input type="date"> fields instead of a custom drill-down calendar. Far less code to build and maintain, and it's a date-entry control everyone already knows, at the cost of a picker UI that's the browser's native chrome rather than something skinned to match the report.

Prototype only — pick a favorite and it'll get wired into the real report.
